questions.q: What is vertical thinking best suited for, according to the summary?
a: Analyzing facts, numbers and data
Dreaming up entirely new products
Solving problems with no precedent
Interpreting emotions within a group
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts vertical thinking with lateral thinking.

questions.q: What does the reversal technique involve?
a: Flipping cause and effect to view a problem from another angle
Listing every possible solution at the same time
Asking a group to vote on the best idea
Repeating one solution until it finally works
questions.why: Lesson 2 says reversing the relationship forces you to rethink it.

questions.q: How should a brainstorming session begin?
a: By sharing ideas without judging them
By ranking the best ideas first
By choosing a leader to make decisions
By writing a formal proposal in advance
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a non-judgmental first stage keeps creativity alive.

a: Trying unfamiliar activities and conversations to train creativity
Reading only the most popular books in your field
Practicing one skill until you have mastered it
Studying statistics carefully before deciding anything
questions.why: Lesson 3 says innovation comes from exploring the unknown and risking failure.

a: Using a random nearby object or word to spark a solution
Following a formal step-by-step planning method
Generating ideas only during scheduled meetings
Writing down every idea and scoring it afterward
questions.why: Lesson 3 says you pick a random tool, word or object and apply it to the problem.
